messages:
maya: Heads-up — after the large nightly batch in us-west2 we saw a sustained NVMe IOPS spike that coincided with the local-consolidator ramping concurrency. GPU provisioning started failing with attach timeouts. :warning:
infra-bot: Alert: nvme-consolidator concurrency=56 on gnode-ctl-47, iops=450k read+write, provisioning-failures=12 (last 10m)
thomas: ugh. did the consolidator start a sweep job or a backlog flush?
maya: It looks like a backlog + immediate post-batch consolidation triggered. The service uses max_workers=64 and backoff=0 by default. When multiple nodes finished batches at once it cascaded.
olivia: can we throttle the consolidator per-node? a soft limit would avoid saturating disk during provisioning windows.
samir: agree. short-term mitigation: set max_workers=8 and add token-bucket rate limit to 200MiB/s. that should prevent attach timeouts while still making progress.
lisa: can we patch without a full deploy? maybe a k8s configmap change + rollout?
thomas: yes, we can patch the k8s Deployment env and do `kubectl rollout restart deploy/local-nvme-consolidator -n infra` to pick it up. I'll prepare the change.
maya: sample config I tested in staging:
```
CONSOLIDATOR_MAX_WORKERS=8
CONSOLIDATOR_RATE_BPS=209715200  # 200 MiB/s
CONSOLIDATOR_COALESCE_WINDOW_MS=3000
```
thomas: rolling restart plan: patch configmap, roll 20% at a time, monitor provisioner attach latencies and nvme iops. if attach latency improves, continue.
infra-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-0421 - post-batch nvme consolidation causing gpu attach timeouts. Link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-0421
olivia: longer-term: make consolidator aware of cluster state (avoid heavy work if scheduler has > N pending gpu pods). can add a scheduler API check before starting heavy passes.
samir: also worth adding jitter to scheduled consolidations and prefer low-traffic windows per-region. this will reduce correlated spikes.
lisa: cost question — throttling slows cleanup and increases ephemeral disk footprint. any rough numbers on storage capacity impact?
maya: rough estimate: with max_workers=8 we saw backlog clear in 18h vs 6h previously for a single node under heavy load. we have spare capacity in most AZs but during peak growth it could push snapshot + retention costs ~2-4% higher. tradeoff seems acceptable for availability.
thomas: will push the config now. monitoring queries to watch: `nvme_ops/sec`, `nvme_bytes/sec`, `gpu_attach_latency_ms`, `provision_fail_rate`. set alert if attach latency > 3000ms.
olivia: thanks — add a runbook entry for on-call: how to temp-throttle and rollback.
maya: already updating runbook in docs-runbook repo. will ping here when done. :thumbsup:
thomas: rollout started (patch applied to configmap). monitoring looks better after first 10% batch. iops down ~60% on affected nodes, attach failures trending to 0. :eyes:
infra-bot: System: rollout complete for 100% (local-nvme-consolidator). No errors reported.
maya: moving to postmortem/proactive work items: 1) consolidate scheduling window by region, 2) add cluster-load check to consolidator, 3) add capacity reservation window for gpu provisioning, 4) dashboard + alert tune. will open tickets.
lisa: nice work. please add cost estimate for extended cleanup so finance can model it.
maya: will do. closing thread for operational actions — leave comments if anything else pops up. :white_check_mark:
